title: Màn hình của tôi bị hỏng
pronunciation: Man hinh cua toi bi hong

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Màn hình của tôi bị hỏng names the problem so staff or a helpful local can act on it.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say Màn hình của tôi bị hỏng calmly and show the proof if you have it: phone screen, charger, SIM card, Wi-Fi screen, or outlet. After that, let the other person ask one follow-up or point you to the right next step.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Build the line around Màn hình của + tôi bị hỏng, then replay the full phrase until the rhythm feels natural.

breakdown.vietnamese: Màn hình của tôi bị hỏng

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Nearby follow-ups: What is the Wi-Fi password?; Do you sell SIM cards?

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this as soon as the problem is clear enough to name. It is especially useful at a counter or desk where someone can look at the photo, receipt, bag, booking, or phone screen with you.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Keep the explanation simple and show the evidence if you can. A short phrase plus a photo, receipt, or booking usually works better than adding more English.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Useful if the exchange continues: My phone battery is dead, Do you have a charger, and Can I charge my phone here.
